morning_concept: Amazon SDE II — System Design: URL Shortener at scale
morning_concept_explanation: A 2026 SDE II candidate report describes a system-design round that started with a URL shortener and then pushed into 10B URLs, click analytics, a redirect-service outage, and hot keys from viral links. Treat this as a real candidate anecdote rather than proof of a recurring Amazon question; the broader Amazon report data shows system design in 30% of 79 SWE reports and coding in 78%. Sources: https://primly.io/c/interview-leaks/thread/primly-human-interview-leaks-x-amazon-sde2-system-design-2026 and https://askedbefore.io/interview/company/amazon. Likely follow-ups: how would you scale reads, handle hot keys, make redirects highly available, and separate analytics from the critical path? What it tests: requirements clarification, capacity thinking, failure handling, caching/partitioning tradeoffs, and communication under follow-up pressure.
evening_feedback: Candidate feedback: recent Amazon SDE/SDE II reports commonly describe a multi-round loop with coding plus behavioral, and system design appears regularly enough to matter for mid-level preparation. The strongest repeated signal is that interviews probe beyond the first workable design: candidates report follow-up drilling on scale, failure modes, and tradeoffs. Separate reports should be treated as corroborating patterns, not guarantees for every team. Sources: https://www.inbyte.org/interview/amazon and https://askedbefore.io/interview/company/amazon. One-off example: an SDE II candidate reported spending about 15 minutes on the high-level URL-shortener design before roughly 30 minutes of edge-case follow-ups.
next_morning_concept: Meta SWE — System Design: compound status-search service
next_morning_concept_explanation: A 2026 Meta senior-SWE candidate report describes a system-design round for a status-search service supporting compound AND/OR queries. Treat it as one candidate report, then use the broader Meta evidence to discuss why design rounds increasingly test requirement clarification, data modeling, query strategy, scale, and tradeoffs. Source: https://www.reddit.com/r/OfferEngineering/comments/1vuk7zu/meta_senior_swe_interview_process_august_2026/; corroborating recent Meta interview reporting: https://www.inbyte.org/interview/meta.
next_evening_feedback: For the Meta follow-up, summarize candidate-reported signals around coding speed, AI-assisted coding, system-design depth, and behavioral follow-ups, while clearly separating repeated themes from individual anecdotes. Ask what changed when the interviewer generalized the problem or added constraints, and what that reveals about the evaluation.
